source_state: Reliability working changes after checkpoint; not a committed or device-measured performance result.

measurement_status.device_audit: The known iPhone 12 Pro was unavailable/offline during the read-only device audit. No sustained FPS, capture cadence, thermal, GPU or room fanout measurements were obtained.

native_eye_capture.requested_format_policy: Prefer advertised 60 Hz at the fewest pixels, else advertised 30 Hz. The selected ARKit format is not proof of achieved native callback cadence.
native_eye_capture.processing: Native face samples enter a bounded ring. Managed Update drains all queued samples, rather than sampling only the latest value. Overflow is explicit and invalidates readiness. A capture timestamp barrier prevents pre-Go blinks from becoming post-Go losses.
native_eye_capture.jpeg_independence: JPEG work is dispatched to a separate serial encode queue with one busy job; busy decorative frames are skipped. Native face-history processing is separate from social-video publication.
native_eye_capture.actual_diagnostics: nativeFPS / requested formatFPS / consumed sample Hz / dropped samples / capture gaps / encode milliseconds / encode busy skips

main_game_render.meaning: Target cadence is not measured FPS. Rendering and transport Tick still share Unity frame time; native sample history preserves intervening eye samples. Offscreen rendering still consumes GPU budget.

social_video.meaning: Decorative room-camera JPEG thumbnails. This received video FPS does not define native blink sampling rate or prove main game FPS.
social_video.stale_behavior: Consent-enabled camera head remains stable with cached frozen image and VIDEO PAUSED indicator. HasLiveFeed means fresh. Explicit camera off/disconnect removes it immediately.
social_video.local_preview_optimization: Optional canonical Texture2D preview is borrowed by Publish, avoiding a second local JPEG decode. Its lifetime remains owned by the camera.

caps_and_assumptions.host_tick_assumption: Transport.Tick once per main game Update. Example Quest host is assumed to achieve 72 FPS; phone host examples assume 30 or 24 FPS. These are capacity scenarios, not observed device rates.
caps_and_assumptions.flush_priority: Reliable gameplay queue/input/snapshot is flushed first. Any reliable backlog blocks camera flushing for that peer on that tick.
caps_and_assumptions.queue_policy: Latest frame coalesces per origin; one round-robin queue slot per origin. Replaced frames do not accumulate into a latency backlog.
caps_and_assumptions.delivery: Fragmentation plus UnreliableSequenced pipeline; dropped fragments can discard an entire JSON thumbnail.
caps_and_assumptions.echo: Compatible host Broadcast includes the origin sender. Owner sequence validation rejects redundant display/decode, but wire delivery and serialization still occur.
caps_and_assumptions.size_interpretation: 8192 bytes is a conservative allowed JSON envelope bound. A max-5000-byte JPEG expands to 6668 Base64 characters plus serialized message fields; actual complete messages may be smaller than the envelope. This report does not claim every frame reaches 8192 bytes.
exclusions: UDP/IP/DTLS/Unity Transport/Relay headers and fragmentation overhead
Real link capacity, contention, packet loss and transport send failures
CPU JSON/Base64 and image-decode cost; GPU texture-upload/render cost

thermal_scenario_caveat: The 24 FPS host row intentionally holds all origins at 6 FPS to isolate the host scheduling limit. If all 16 origins are thermally limited to 4 FPS, desired per-peer rate is 64 messages/s, still above the 48 messages/s host flush ceiling; the fair-share upper bound remains 3 FPS/origin. The host thermal state does not imply every remote origin is thermal-limited.

scaling_assessment.phone_16_camera_fanout: 16 origins at 6 FPS require 96 camera messages/s per recipient; a 30 FPS phone host can flush at most 60. Even an ideal fair share is 3.75 FPS/origin before other limits. Compatible self-echo consumes part of that budget.
scaling_assessment.cpu_work_example: A Quest host receiving 15 phone streams at 6 FPS may accept/decode up to 90 remote JPEG frames/s. Each recipient may decode the other 15 origins up to 90 times/s if transport permits. This is workload count, not measured CPU cost.
scaling_assessment.fluid_video_requirement: Increasing the JSON/JPEG publication number alone is not a sound route to fluid 16-phone video: fanout scales as origins times peers and each frame repeats Base64/JSON, JPEG decode and GPU upload. Fluid video at this scale needs a separately designed media path with hardware codecs, congestion/adaptation, selective subscriptions and appropriate server/media fanout, such as a WebRTC-based design.
scaling_assessment.implemented_scope: Current changes improve blink-history correctness, reduce local decode work, limit phone mirror cost and expose honest frozen/stale state. A hardware-codec/media-transport replacement is not implemented or claimed.
